newsitem.title: FRANCE: France presses child abuse campaign, porn charges.
newsitem.headline: France presses child abuse campaign, porn charges.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe launched a national campaign against child abuse on Thursday as justice officials charged 36 people held in a crackdown with suspected child pornography offences.
Almost 250 people have been detained and 5,000 cassettes seized -- including one involving a six-month-old baby -- in a nationwide clampdown on paedophile videos begun on Wednesday.
By Thursday afternoon, 170 of those detained had been released and investigators had not managed to identify the makers of the videos, a public prosecutor said.

Most of the suspects, who included schoolteachers, a social worker and a child day-care centre manager, were placed under investigation for "possession of pornographic material related to the sexual abuse of minors", police said.
Juppe declared the fight against maltreatment of children a "great national cause", inaugurating an information campaign designed to raise awareness of the extent of the problem.

"We are probably going to have new atrocities in the headlines as we have had in the last few weeks and months. Other tragedies and other crimes will be discovered because that is the evil way of the world," he told a news conference.

"Unless we mobilise the whole country, unless all French people become more aware and committed, we will not achieve our aim, although we see from the revelation of the latest tragedies that the task is enormous," the prime minister said.
The government-funded campaign by 16 child welfare associations features posters, television advertising spots and a free telephone helpline with the number 119.
After watching revelations of paedophile murder and rape cases engulf neighbouring Belgium, France is now uncovering its own child sex scandals.
A sales representative arrested last weekend after allegedly attempting to abduct a schoolgirl is reported by police to have confessed to nine unsolved sexual assaults on minors.

And a 32-year-old Frenchman on trial for possessing child pornography cited the single European market in his defence to a court in Saint-Gaudens, southwestern France, saying that if he could not lawfully possess in France kiddy-porn videos he had bought legally in Germany, "it makes a nonsense of Europe".
Investigators said many of the men arrested in this week's swoop were married with children of their own.
"The suspects are all men, from all social classes," said gendarmerie officer Patrick Gens at the headquarters of the investigation in Nice, on the the French Riviera.
The probe headed by investigating magistrate Jean-Pierre Rousseau began last October when a driving school instructor was arrested in possession of a dozen paedophile videos.

Three more people were detained in January and searches of their homes enabled investigators to draw up a list of suspected clients, who bought videos via the national Minitel telephone computer network and the Internet.
According to official figures, 20,000 cases of maltreatment of children were reported to French social services in 1995, including 7,000 cases of violence and 5,500 of sexual abuse.
Another 10,000 to 15,000 cases were reported directly to the justice authorities by schools, police, hospitals and private citizens.
